content: For the treatment of infections caused by Staphylococcus haemolyticus: 1. Methicillin-susceptible strains: The first-line treatment options include: Nafcillin administered intravenously at a dose of 1–2 grams every 4–6 hours, with a maximum daily dose of 12 grams. Oxacillin administered intravenously at a dose of 1–2 grams every 4–6 hours, with a maximum daily dose of 12 grams. Cefazolin administered intravenously at a dose of 0.5–2 grams every 6–8 hours. Alternative treatment options include: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) administered intravenously at a dose of 4–5 mg/kg every 6–12 hours. Doxycycline administered intravenously at a dose of 100–200 mg every 12–24 hours. 2. Methicillin-resistant, glycopeptide-susceptible strains: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15–20 mg/kg every 8–12 hours. 3. Methicillin-resistant, glycopeptide-resistant strains: The first-line treatment options include: Daptomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 4–6 mg/kg every 24 hours. Linezolid administered either orally or intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 12 hours. For infections caused by Staphylococcus saprophyticus: 1. Urinary tract infections: The preferred treatment options include: Cephalexin administered orally at a dose of 500 mg four times daily. Amoxicillin-clavulanate administered orally at a dose of 875/125 mg twice daily. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) administered orally at a dose of 160–800 mg twice daily. An alternative treatment option is Levofloxacin administered orally at a dose of 500 mg once daily. For infections caused by Streptococcus anginosus: 1. Dental abscesses: The preferred treatment is Penicillin V administered orally at a dose of 500 mg four times daily. An alternative treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15–20 mg/kg every 8–12 hours. 2. Brain abscesses: The first-line treatment options include: Penicillin G administered intravenously at a total daily dose of 18–24 million units, divided into doses every 4–6 hours. Ceftriaxone administered intravenously at a dose of 2 grams every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15–20 mg/kg every 8–12 hours. For infections caused by Bacillus cereus: 1. Food poisoning: Antibiotic therapy is not required as the condition is typically self-limiting. 2. Bacteremia: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin administered intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 8 hours. Note: Bacillus cereus is often resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics. Pseudobacteremia is usually transient and results from contamination of blood cultures, gloves, or syringes. 3. Meningitis or brain abscesses: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin administered intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 8 hours. Note: Blood culture isolates are often contaminants unless proven otherwise, particularly in intravenous drug users. 4. Endophthalmitis: The preferred treatment involves: Intravitreal administration of Clindamycin at a dose of 450 μg and Gentamicin at a dose of 400 μg, or Dexamethasone intravitreal injection. Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin administered intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 8 hours. Note: Management requires ophthalmological consultation, culturing of ocular fluids, early vitrectomy, and intravitreal antibiotics. 5. Endocarditis: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. Note: Blood cultures in intravenous drug users are often contaminants or represent transient bacteremia. 6. Soft tissue infections: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin administered intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 8 hours. 7. Pneumonia: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin administered intravenously at a dose of 600 mg every 8 hours. For infections caused by Elizabethkingia meningoseptica: 1. Bacteremia: The first-line treatment options include: Levofloxacin administered either intravenously or orally at a dose of 750 mg every 24 hours. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) administered intravenously at a total daily dose of 8–10 mg/kg, divided into doses every 6–8 hours. Alternative treatment options include: Ciprofloxacin administered intravenously at a dose of 400 mg every 12 hours. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) administered intravenously at a total daily dose of 8–10 mg/kg, divided into doses every 6–8 hours.
